q: 1. The amount of water used for one kilograms distemper is
explain: Approximately 0.6 litre of water is typically used to mix with 1 kg of distemper powder.

q: 2. PVC stands for
explain: PVC is the common abbreviation for polyvinyl chloride, a widely used plastic polymer.

q: 3. What indicates for 80/100 in case of bitumen?
options: Penetration residue from loss on heating of bitumen
explain: The 80/100 notation refers to the penetration grade, indicating the depth (in tenths of mm) a needle penetrates the bitumen sample under standard conditions.

q: 4. The ingredient which gives the desired colour to a paint is called
explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide color, opacity, and some level of protection in paint.

q: 5. The paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
explain: White lead base is excellent for wood because it is very durable and flexible, but it is rarely used on iron as it can promote corrosion compared to red lead.

q: 6. The function of base of an oil paint is
options: to form the body of the paint
to reinforce the film of the paint after drying
to prevent penetration of paint to lower surfaces
explain: The 'base' (like white lead or zinc oxide) provides the bulk or body of the paint and determines its character.

q: 7. The vehicle used in case of enamel paints is
explain: As per key but Enamel paint is essentially a mixture of pigment and varnish, which gives it a hard, glossy finish.

q: 8. The main component of oil paint is
explain: Oil paint requires a base/pigment, a vehicle (carrier), and a thinner (like turpentine) to be effective.

q: 9. The pigment in paints gives
explain: The primary role of the pigment is to provide color and hide the surface being painted.

q: 10. Base pigments are used for
explain: The base is a solid substance in a fine state of division and forms the bulk of a paint. It imparts durability and protects the surface from weathering.

q: 11. Extenders used in paints for
explain: Extenders (or fillers) are added to paint to increase its volume and make it spread more easily, which helps in reducing the overall cost.

q: 12. The commonly used thinner in oil paints is
explain: Both Naphtha and Turpentine are common thinners used to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints for better workability.

q: 13. The commonly used thinner in distempers
explain: Distemper is a water-based paint, therefore water is used as the thinning agent to achieve the desired consistency.

q: 14. The defect in painting over a smooth and glossy surface due to which paint does not stick to the surface, is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when gas or moisture is trapped under the paint film, often because it fails to adhere to a smooth or glossy surface.

q: 15. The base material for distemper is
explain: Chalk (whiting) is the primary base material used in the preparation of distemper.

q: 16. Distemper is a mixture of
explain: Basic distemper consists of powdered chalk mixed with water and a binder (like glue/size).

q: 17. Vehicle not used in paint is
explain: Turpentine oil is a thinner, not a vehicle (carrier oil). Linseed, poppy, and tung oils are all common vehicles.

q: 18. The paint highly resistant to fire is
explain: Asbestos is naturally fire-resistant; hence, asbestos paint is used to protect surfaces from fire hazards.

q: 19. Bitumen 80/100 indicates
options: Penetration of residue from loss on heating
explain: The 80/100 designation specifies the penetration grade of bitumen, a measure of its hardness/consistency.

q: 20. The oily liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form a paint is called
explain: The vehicle (or binder) is the liquid that holds the pigment and base in suspension and helps it adhere to the surface.

q: 21. The base in a paint has the following function
options: it forms the body of the paint
it reinforces the films of the paint after it has dried
explain: The base provides bulk, prevents shrinkage, and gives strength to the dried paint film.

q: 22. The cracks in the painted surface extending throughout the thickness of the paint are caused due to
options: improper seasoning of the painted wood
too many coats of paint resulting in excessive thickness
explain: Deep cracks can be caused by wood movement, chemical imbalances from driers, or mechanical stress from overly thick layers.

q: 23. The small areas on painted surface enclosed by hair line cracks are called
explain: Crazing refers to the formation of fine, shallow hairline cracks on the surface of the paint.

q: 24. Lacquer paints are
options: are more durable compared to enamel paints
explain: Lacquers are high-performance coatings often containing nitrocellulose and resins, known for their durability on metal surfaces.

q: 25. Asphalt is a mixture of
explain: Asphalt is formed by combining bitumen with inert mineral matter such as sand, gravel, or limestone dust.

q: 26. Lacquer is
explain: Lacquers are technically a type of spirit varnish that dries by evaporation of the solvent.

q: 27. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surfaces not exposed to weather
explain: Distemper is not weather-resistant and is primarily used for interior walls (interior plastered surfaces).

q: 28. The best primer used for structural steel/iron is
explain: Red lead is the most effective primer for steel as it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

q: 29. Distemper paint means
explain: Distemper is fundamentally a water-based paint made from chalk, pigment, and a glue/water binder.

q: 30. The paint used for automobiles is
explain: Modern automobile finishes often use advanced oil-based paints for a smooth, durable finish.

q: 31. Duco is the trade name for
explain: Duco is a well-known brand of cellulose-based paint commonly used in the automotive industry.

q: 32. The paint which gives illumination during night is called
explain: Fluorescent or luminescent paints contain pigments that glow in the dark or reflect light intensely.

q: 33. The function of a paint is
options: to increase the life of the surface
explain: Paint serves both aesthetic (appearance) and protective (corrosion/weathering) functions.

q: 34. The painting work is generally specified by
explain: In engineering estimates, painting work is measured and specified in terms of surface area (square meters/feet).

q: 35. The paints used in aircrafts are
explain: Cellulose paints (lacquers) are used for aircraft because they dry very rapidly by evaporation and provide a hard, smooth, and flexible surface.

q: 36. The main constituent of varnish is
explain: Resins (like amber, copal, or shellac) are the primary solid constituent of varnish that forms the protective film.

q: 37. The varnish is essentially made of
explain: Varnish consists of a resin dissolved in a solvent (and sometimes oil) to allow for application and film formation.

q: 38. French polish is made by dissolving the resin
explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in methylated spirit.

q: 39. Snowcem is
explain: Snowcem is a well-known commercial brand name for waterproof cement-based paint.

q: 40. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance is
explain: Red lead (lead tetroxide) is highly effective at preventing the corrosion of iron and steel.

q: 41. The pigment commonly used in the manufacture
explain: Ambers (browns), Iron Oxide (reds/browns), and Lamp Black (blacks) are all standard pigments used to provide color to paint.

q: 42. PVC controls in paint
explain: Pigment Volume Concentration (PVC) affects nearly all physical properties of the paint film, including its sheen and strength.

q: 43. PVC stands for
explain: In the context of paint technology, PVC refers to the Pigment Volume Concentration.

q: 44. Muller is concerned with
explain: A muller is a tool (often stone) used to grind and mix pigments with a vehicle during paint preparation.

q: 45. The cracks developed throughout thickness of paint due various reason is known as
explain: Cracking involves deep breaks in the paint film that often expose the underlying surface.

q: 46. The material generally not used as extender in paints is
explain: Zinc white is a primary pigment (base), whereas silica, gypsum, and talc are inert materials used as extenders.

q: 47. The following element of a paint is used as base, pigment as well as drier
explain: Red lead is unique because it serves as a base, provides color (pigment), and acts as an oxidizing drier.

q: 48. Stucco paints are suitable for
explain: Stucco paints are specifically designed for external masonry surfaces like stone and brick.

q: 49. The radiator of vehicles are pointed with
explain: Bronze or aluminum paints are used for radiators due to their high thermal conductivity and heat resistance.

q: 50. Inert filler / adulterant is used in paint to
explain: Inert fillers (extenders) are used to bulk up the paint and make it more economical.
